nodes.name: Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement:
\textup{(a)} Let $\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D}' \in\mathscr{P}(\mathscr{P}(\Theta))$ such that
$\int
P \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{D}= G$
and $\int P \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{D}' = G'$. For $r \geq1$, if $W_r(\mathcal{D}
,\mathcal{D}')$
is finite
then $W_r(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D}') \geq W_r(G,G')$.

\textup{(b)} Let $\mathcal{D}= \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G}$ and $\mathcal{D}' = \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G'}$.
Then $W_r(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D}') = W_r(G,G')$ if both quantities are finite.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement:
\textup{(a)} Under assumption \textup{(A1)},

\begin{eqnarray*}
K({p_{Y_{[n]}|G}},{p_{Y_{[n]}|G'}}) & \leq&
C_1 n W_r^r \bigl(G,G' \bigr),
\\
h^2({p_{Y_{[n]}|G}},{p_{Y_{[n]}|G'}}) &
\leq& C_1 n W_{2r}^{2r} \bigl(G,G'
\bigr),
\\
h^2({p_{Y_{[n]}|G}},{p_{Y_{[n]}|G'}}) &
\leq& V({p_{Y_{[n]}|G}},{p_{Y_{[n]}|G'}}) \leq \sqrt
{1 - \bigl(1- C_1 W_{2r}^{2r}
\bigl(G,G' \bigr) \bigr)^n}.
\end{eqnarray*}

\textup{(b)} Under assumption \textup{(A2)}, we have $\upchi(
{p_{Y_{[n]}|G}},{p_{Y_{[n]}|G'}}) \leq M^n$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.3: Lem-entropy
nodes.statement:
\textup{(a)} Under assumption \textup{(A1)}, for any $\upvarepsilon\in(0,1/2)$,

\[
\log N \bigl(\upvarepsilon, \bigl\{{p_{Y_{[n]}|G}}| G \in \mathscr{P}(
\Theta) \bigr\}, h \bigr) \leq \bigl(2C_1 n \operatorname{diam}(
\Theta)/\upvarepsilon^2 \bigr)^{d} \log \bigl( \mathrm{e}+
2\mathrm{e}C_1 n \operatorname{diam}(\Theta)/\upvarepsilon^2 \bigr).
\]

\textup{(b)} Under assumption \textup{(A1)}, for any $\upvarepsilon\in(0,1/2)$, $k \in
\mathbb{N}$,

\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\log N \bigl(\upvarepsilon, \{{p_{Y_{[n]}|G}}| G \mbox { has } k
\mbox{ support points on } \Theta\}, h \bigr)
\\
&&\quad\leq kd\log \bigl(2C_1 n \operatorname{diam}(\Theta)/
\upvarepsilon^2 \bigr) + \log \bigl(\mathrm{e}+ 2\mathrm{e}C_1 n
\operatorname{diam}(\Theta)/ \upvarepsilon^2 \bigr).
\end{eqnarray*}

\textup{(c)} If $f$ is a Gaussian kernel on $\mathbb{R}^d$,
$f(x) = \frac{1}{(2\uppi)^{d/2}\upsigma^{d}}
\mathrm{e}^{-\|x\|^2/2\upsigma^2}$, for some $\upsigma>0$, then

\[
\log N \bigl(\upvarepsilon, \bigl\{{p_{Y_{[n]}|G}}| G \in \mathscr{P}(
\Theta) \bigr\}, h \bigr) \lesssim \bigl(\log(1/\upvarepsilon) \bigr)^{2d+1}n^{2d}
\log n,
\]

where the multiplying constant depends only on $d, \upsigma, \Theta$
(and not on $n$).

nodes.name: Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $\operatorname{law}(G) = \mathscr{D}_{\upgamma H}$, where $H$ is a nonatomic probability
measure on $\Theta$. For a small $\upvarepsilon> 0$, let $D =
D(\upvarepsilon
,\Theta,\|\cdot\|)$
the packing number of $\Theta$ under $\|\cdot\|$. Then, for any $G_0
\in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$,

\[
\mathbb{P} \bigl(G\dvt W_r^r(G_0,G) \leq \bigl(2^r
+ 1 \bigr)\upvarepsilon^r \bigr) \geq\frac{\Gamma(\upgamma) \upgamma
^{D}}{(2D)^{D-1}} \biggl(
\frac{\upvarepsilon}{\operatorname{diam}(\Theta)} \biggr)^{r(D-1)} \sup_{S} \prod
_{i=1}^{D} H(S_i).
\]

Here, $(S_1,\ldots, S_D)$ denotes the $D$ disjoint $\upvarepsilon/2$-balls
that form
a maximal packing of $\Theta$.
$\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function. The
supremum is taken over all packings $S:= (S_1,\ldots, S_D)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement:
Given assumptions \textup{(A1)--(A3)}, $\Theta$ a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$.

\begin{longlist}[(a)]

\item[(a)] Let $D := (\operatorname{diam}(\Theta))^d (n^3/\updelta^2)^{d/r}$
and constants $c, C$ depending only on $C_1, M, \upeta_0, \upgamma,\break
\operatorname{diam}(\Theta)$ and $r$. Then,
for any $G_0 \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$,
$\updelta> 0$ and $n > C\log(1/\updelta)$, the following
inequality holds under the probability measure $\mathcal{D}_{\upgamma H}$:

\[
\log\mathbb{P} \bigl(G \in B_K(G_0,\updelta) \bigr) \geq c \log \bigl[
\upgamma^D \bigl(\updelta^2/n^3
\bigr)^{(1+d/r)(D-1) + Dd/r} \bigr].
\]

\item[(b)] If in addition, $G_0$ has exactly $k$ support points in
$\Theta$,
then

\[
\log\mathbb{P} \bigl(G \in B_K(G_0,\updelta) \bigr) \geq c \log \bigl[
\upgamma^k \bigl(\updelta^2/n^3
\bigr)^{kd/r + k/r} \bigl(1/k\operatorname{diam}\Theta^r
\bigr)^{k} \bigr].
\]

\item[(c)] If $f$ is the Gaussian kernel (given in Lemma~3.3),
then for any $G_0 \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$, the bound in part \textup{(b)} of the lemma
continues to hold with $k \lesssim(\log(1/\updelta))^{2d}(nd)^{2d}$.
\end{longlist}

nodes.name: Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement:
Let $\Theta$ be a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and
$G_0 \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$. Given assumptions \textup{(A1)--(A3)},
parameters $\upalpha> 0, \upgamma> 0$ and $H \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ are known.
Let $m$ tend to infinity, while $n$ can be either fixed to a constant,
or $n$ tending to infinity at a rate relatively to $m$.
Then there is a large constant $C$ independent of both $m$ and $n$ such that
the posterior induced by the model of equations (9)
and (10)
satisfies

\[
\Pi_G \biggl(h({p_{Y_{[n]}|G_0}},
{p_{Y_{[n]}|G}}) \geq C \biggl[\frac{n^{3d}\log(mn)}{m} \biggr]^{1/(2d+2)} \Big|
Y_{[n]}^{[m]} \biggr) \longrightarrow0
\]

in $P_{Y_{[n]}|G_0}^m$-probability. Moreover,

\begin{longlist}[(ii)]

\item[(i)] If $f$ is a Gaussian kernel with a fixed variance, then the
rate is improved to

\[
\upvarepsilon_{mn}= \biggl[\frac{n^{2d}(\log m)^{2d+1}\log n}{m} \biggr]^{1/2}.
\]

\item[(ii)] If $G_0$ has a finite \emph{and} known number of support points,
then the rate is improved to

\[
\upvarepsilon_{mn}= \biggl[\frac{\log(mn)}{m} \biggr]^{1/2}.
\]

\end{longlist}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}= \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G}$, where $G = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \upbeta_i
\updelta
_{\uptheta_i}$
for some $k < \infty$, $\upalpha, \upalpha' > 0$.
Define

\[
\mathscr{C}= \bigl\{\mathscr{D}_{\upalpha'G'} | G' \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta), \operatorname{spt}
G' = \operatorname{spt} G \bigr\}.
\]

\begin{longlist}[(a)]

\item[(a)]
If $\min_{i} \upalpha\upbeta_i \geq1$, then
$\mathscr{C}$ has \emph{strong} $r$-regular boundary with respect to
$\mathcal{D}$.

\item[(b)] If $\max_{i} \upalpha\upbeta_i < 1$,
then
$\mathscr{C}$ has \emph{strong} ${\upalpha^*}r$-regular boundary with
respect to $\mathcal{D}$,
where ${\upalpha^*}= \min_{i} \upalpha\upbeta_i$.
\end{longlist}

nodes.name: Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $\Theta$ is bounded.
Let $\mathcal{D}= \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G}$, where $G= \sum_{i=1}^{k}\upbeta_i \updelta
_{\uptheta_i}$ for
some $k < \infty$ and $\upalpha\in(0,1]$. Let $\upalpha_1 > \upalpha_0 > 0$
be given. Define

\[
\mathscr{C}= \bigl\{ \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha' G'} | G' \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta);
\upalpha' \in[\upalpha_0,\upalpha_1] \bigr\}.
\]

Then $\mathscr{C}$ has $\upalpha^* r$-regular boundary with respect to
$\mathcal{D}$,
where $\upalpha^* = \min_{i} \upalpha\upbeta_i$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.2
nodes.statement:
Assume that $\mathcal{D}=\mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G}$ for some $\upalpha\in(0,1]$.
$\operatorname{spt} G$ is a $(c_1,c_2,K)$-sparse subset of a bounded space $\Theta$
and that $G$ is a sparse measure equipped with gauge function $g$.
Let $\upalpha_1 \geq\upalpha_0 > 0$.
Then,
for any $\mathcal{D}' \in\mathscr{C}$, where

\[
\mathscr{C}= \bigl\{\mathcal{D}' = \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha'G'} | G'
\in\mathscr{P}(\Theta), \upalpha' \in[\upalpha_0,
\upalpha_1] \bigr\}
\]

there exists a measurable set $\mathscr{B}\subset\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ for which

\begin{longlist}[(ii)]

\item[(i)] $\mathcal{D}'(\mathscr{B}) - \mathcal{D}(\mathscr{B}) \gtrsim W_r^r(G,G')$,

\item[(ii)] for any $\updelta\lesssim W_r(G,G')$,

\[
\mathcal{D}(\mathscr{B}_\updelta\setminus\mathscr{B}) \lesssim24^{K(c_0W_r(G,G'))} \times \biggl(
\frac{\updelta}{W_r(G,G')} \biggr)^{\upalpha rg
(c_0W_r(G,G'))}.
\]

\end{longlist}

Here, $c_0$ and the multiplying
constants in $\lesssim$ and $\gtrsim$ depend only on $\mathcal{D}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement:
Suppose that assumption \textup{(A1)} holds for some $r\geq1, C_1 > 0$. Let $\upeta
_n$ satisfy
$\upeta_n \leq c_1\upvarepsilon_n^2$, $\upvarepsilon_n \rightarrow0$ at a
rate to
be specified.
Then the $\upeta_n$-MLE satisfies
the following bound under $Q_0*f$-measure, for any $Q_0 \in\mathcal{Q}$:




\begin{eqnarray}
\mathbb{P} \bigl(h(\hat{f}_n,Q_0*f) \geq\upvarepsilon_n
\bigr) & \leq& 5\exp \bigl(-c_2n\upvarepsilon_n^2
\bigr),
\\
 \mathbb{P} \bigl(W_2(\hat{Q}_n,Q_0)
\geq\updelta_n \bigr) & \leq& 5\exp \bigl(-c_2n
\upvarepsilon_n^2 \bigr),
\end{eqnarray}

where $c_1,c_2$ are some universal positive constants. $\upvarepsilon_n$ and
$\updelta_n$
are given as follows:

\begin{longlist}[(a)]

\item[(a)] $\upvarepsilon_n = C_2(\log n/n)^{r/2d}$, if $d > 2r$;
$\upvarepsilon_n = C_2(\log n/n)^{r/(d+2r)}$ if $d<2r$, and
$\upvarepsilon_n =  (\log n)^{3/4}/n^{1/4}$ if $d=2r$.

\item[(b)] $\upvarepsilon_n = C_2 n^{-1/2}\log n$, if $\mathcal{Q}= \mathcal{Q}_k$
and $\mathcal{F}= \mathcal{F}_k$ for some $k < \infty$.

\item[(c)] If $f$
is ordinary smooth with parameter $\upbeta> 0$,
then $\updelta_n = C_3 \upvarepsilon_n^{{1}/{(2+\upbeta d')}}$ for any
$d' > d$.

\item[(d)] If $f$
is supersmooth with parameter $\upbeta> 0$, then
$\updelta_n = C_3 [-\log\upvarepsilon_n]^{-1/\upbeta}$.
\end{longlist}

Here, $C_2,C_3$ are different constants in each case. $C_2$
depends only on $d,r,\Theta$ and $C_1$, while $C_3$ depends only on
$d,\upbeta, \Theta$ and $C_2$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $\Theta$ is a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$, \textup{(A1)} holds for
some $C_1 > 0$ and some $r \in[1,2]$.
Let $\updelta_n$ and $\upvarepsilon_n$ be vanishing sequences
for which equation (26) holds.
Fix $G\in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ and $\upalpha\in(0,1]$, while $G'$ varies in
$\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$.
Let ${\upalpha^*}= \upalpha\inf_{\uptheta\in\operatorname{spt} G}G(\{\uptheta\})$.
Then there are
positive constants
$c_0,c_1,C_0$ depending only on $G$, and $c_2>0$ a universal constant, such
that for any $G' \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$, $\upalpha' \in[\upalpha_1,\upalpha
_0]$ given
and $n$ sufficiently large so that $\updelta_n \lesssim W_r(G,G')$, the
following holds:



\begin{equation}
 c_0W_r^r \bigl(G,G' \bigr)
\leq V(P_{Y_{[n]}|G},P_{Y_{[n]}|G'}) + 10\exp \bigl(-c_2 n
\upvarepsilon_n^2 \bigr) + A_n \bigl(W_r
\bigl(G,G' \bigr) \bigr),
\end{equation}

where $A_n(W_r(G,G'))$ takes the form:



\begin{equation}
 A_n(\upomega) = \cases{ C_0(2
\updelta_n/\upomega)^{{\upalpha^*}r}, & \quad $ \mbox{if } G \mbox{ has finite
support,}$\vspace*{2pt}
\cr
C_024^{K(c_1\upomega)}(2
\updelta_n/\upomega)^{\upalpha rg(c_1\upomega)}, &\quad $\mbox{if } G \mbox { is } (
\upgamma_1,\upgamma_2,K)\mbox{-sparse with gauge $g$}$.}
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement:
Let $\Theta$ be a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $G_0 \in\mathscr{P}
(\Theta
)$. Given
assumptions \textup{(A1)}--\textup{(A3)}, parameters $\upalpha\in(0,1],
\upgamma> 0$ and $H \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ are known.
Then, as $m \rightarrow\infty$ and $n = n(m) \rightarrow\infty$,
there is a sequence $\upvarepsilon_{mn}$ and $\Delta_n$ dependent on $m$ and $n$
such that
under the model given equations~(9) and (10),
there holds:

\[
\Pi_G \bigl(W_1(G,G_0) \leq C (\upvarepsilon_{mn}+
\Delta_n) | Y_{[n]}^{[m]} \bigr) \longrightarrow1
\]

in $P_{Y_{[n]}|G_0}^m$-probability for a large constant $C$ independent of
$m$ and $n$.
In particular,
$\upvarepsilon_{mn}$ is any posterior concentration rate for the marginal
densities such as the ones established by Theorem~2.1.
Regarding the nature of $\Delta_n$,

\begin{longlist}[(iii)]

\item[(i)] If $G_0$ has finite (but unknown) number of support points, then

\[
\Delta_n \asymp\updelta_n^{{\upalpha^*}/({\upalpha^*}+1)}.
\]

\item[(ii)] If $G_0$ has infinite and supersparse support with parameters
$(\upgamma_0,\upgamma_1)$, then

\[
\Delta_n \asymp\exp- \bigl[\log(1/\updelta_n)
\bigr]^{1/(1\vee\upgamma_0 +\upgamma_1)}.
\]

\item[(iii)] If $G_0$ has infinite and ordinary sparse support with parameters
$(\upgamma_0,\upgamma_1)$, then

\[
\Delta_n \asymp \bigl[\log(1/\updelta_n)
\bigr]^{-1/(\upgamma_0+\upgamma_1)}.
\]

\end{longlist}

nodes.name: Lemma 6.1
nodes.statement:
Given $G_0 = \sum_{i=1}^{k}\upbeta_i \updelta_{\uptheta_{i}}$ and small
$\upvarepsilon> 0$.
Let $G \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ such that $W_1(G,G_0) \leq\upvarepsilon$.
Suppose that $\operatorname{law}(Q) = \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G}$, where $\upalpha\in(0,1]$.

\begin{longlist}[(a)]

\item[(a)] For any $Q_0 \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ such that $\operatorname{spt} Q_0
\subset\operatorname{spt} G_0$,
and any $\updelta$ such that $\updelta\geq\max_{i\leq k} 2\upvarepsilon
/\upbeta
_i$ and
$\updelta\leq\min_{i,j\leq k} \|\uptheta_i-\uptheta_j\|/2$, any $r\geq1$,
there holds

\[
\mathbb{P} \bigl(W_r(Q_0,Q) \leq2^{1/r}\updelta \bigr) \geq\Gamma(
\upalpha) (\upalpha/2)^k \biggl(\frac{\updelta^r}{2k \operatorname
{diam}(\Theta)} \biggr)^{\upalpha+ k-1}
\prod_{i=1}^{k}\upbeta_i.
\]

\item[(b)] In addition, suppose that \textup{(A1)--(A2)} hold for some $r \geq1$.
Then, there are constants $C, c>0$ depending only on $\upalpha, k, C_1,
M, \operatorname{diam}(\Theta), r$
and $\upbeta_i$'s such that
for any $\updelta$ such that $\updelta/\log(1/\updelta) \geq C\upvarepsilon^{r/2}$,

\[
\mathbb{P} \bigl(Q \in B_K(Q_0, \updelta) \bigr) \geq c
\bigl( \updelta/\log(1/\updelta) \bigr)^{2(\upalpha+k-1)}.
\]

\end{longlist}

nodes.name: Lemma 6.2
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}:= \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G}$ and $r\geq1$. For any $\updelta> 0$,
and for any $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$, there is a
measurable set $\mathcal{B}_k\subset\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ satisfies
the following properties:

\begin{longlist}[(a)]

\item[(a)] $\sup_{Q\in\mathcal{B}_k} \inf_{Q'\in\mathcal{Q}_k} W_r
(Q,Q') \leq
\updelta$.

\item[(b)] $\log N(\updelta, \mathcal{B}_k, W_r)
\leq k(\log N(\updelta/4, \Theta, \|\cdot\|) + \log(e+ 4e\operatorname{diam}
(\Theta
)^r/\updelta^r))$.

\item[(c)] There holds




\[
\mathcal{D} \bigl(\mathscr{P}(\Theta) \setminus\mathcal{B}_k \bigr) \leq
 k^{-k} \bigl(\updelta/\operatorname{diam}(\Theta) \bigr)^{\upalpha r} \bigl[e\upalpha
r \log \bigl(\operatorname{diam}(\Theta)/\updelta \bigr) \bigr]^k.
\]












\end{longlist}

nodes.name: Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement:
Given $\upvarepsilon> 0$, $k < \infty, r\geq1$.
Let $G_0, G \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ such that $G_0$ has $k$ support
points and $W_1(G,G_0) \leq\upvarepsilon$.
Let $\mathcal{D}:= \mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G}$ for some $\upalpha> 0$. For any $\updelta> 0$,
there is a measurable set $\mathcal{B}\subset\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ that
satisfies the
following:

\begin{longlist}[(a)]

\item[(a)] $\log N(\updelta, \mathcal{B}, W_r) \leq k(\log N(\updelta/4,
\Theta,
\|\cdot\|)
+ \log(e+4e\operatorname{diam}(\Theta)^r/\updelta^r))$.

\item[(b)] $\mathcal{D}(\mathscr{P}(\Theta) \setminus\mathcal{B}) \leq\upvarepsilon
\operatorname{diam}
(\Theta)^{r-1}/\updelta^r$.
\end{longlist}

nodes.statement: Cited: Nguyen-11  (Theorem 4)

nodes.name: Lemma 6.4
nodes.statement:
Let $\Theta$ be a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$.
Assumptions \textup{(A1)--(A2)} hold.
Let $Q_0 \in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ such that $\operatorname{spt} Q_0 \subset\operatorname{spt} G_0$,
where $G_0 = \sum_{i=1}^{k}\upbeta_i \updelta_{\uptheta_i}$ for some $k
<\infty$.
Let $\Pi_G$ be an arbitrary prior distribution on $\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$.
Consider the following hierarchical model:

\begin{eqnarray*}
G \sim\Pi_G, Q|G &\sim& \Pi_Q :=
\mathscr{D}_{\upalpha G},
\\
Y_{[n]}= (Y_1,\ldots, Y_n)| Q & \stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}} {\sim} &
Q*f.
\end{eqnarray*}

Let $\upvarepsilon_n \downarrow0$ and define
events $\mathcal{E}_n:= \{W_1(G,G_0) \leq\upvarepsilon_n\}$.
Then the posterior distribution of $Q$ given $Y_{[n]}$
admits the following as $n\rightarrow\infty$:




\begin{eqnarray}
 \Pi_{Q} \bigl(h(Q*f,Q_0*f)\geq
\updelta_{n} | Y_{[n]}, \mathcal{E}_n \bigr) &\rightarrow&0,
\\
 \Pi_{Q} \bigl(W_2(Q,Q_0)\geq
M_n\updelta_{n} | Y_{[n]}, \mathcal{E}_n \bigr)
&\rightarrow& 0
\end{eqnarray}

in $(Q_0*f) \times\Pi_G$-probability, where the rates $\updelta_n$
and $M_n\updelta_n$ are given as follows:

\begin{longlist}[(iii)]

\item[(i)] $\updelta_n \asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(d+2)}+ \upvarepsilon
_n^{r/2}\log
(1/\upvarepsilon_n)$.

\item[(ii)] If $f$ is ordinary smooth with smoothness $\upbeta> 0$,
$M_n\updelta_n \asymp\updelta_n^{{1}/{(2+\upbeta d')}}$ for any $d'>d$.

\item[(iii)] If $f$ is supersmooth with smoothness $\upbeta> 0$, then
$M_n \updelta_n \asymp(-\log\updelta_n)^{-1/\upbeta}$.
\end{longlist}

If $\upvarepsilon_n \downarrow0$ suitably fast, then the following
rates for $\updelta_n$ are valid:

\begin{longlist}[(iii)]

\item[(iv)] If $f$ is ordinary smooth,
and $\upvarepsilon_n \rightarrow0$ sufficiently fast such that
$\upvarepsilon_n \lesssim n^{-(\upalpha+k+4M_0)}\times\break   (\log n)^{-(\upalpha
+k-2)}$, where
$M_0$ is some large constant,
then $\updelta_n \asymp(\log n/n)^{1/2}$.

\item[(v)] If $f$ is supersmooth with smoothness $\upbeta> 0$,
and $\upvarepsilon_n \rightarrow0$ sufficiently fast such that
$\upvarepsilon_n \lesssim n^{-2(\upalpha+k)/(\upbeta+2)} (\log
n)^{-2(\upalpha+k-1)}
\exp(-4n^{\upbeta/(\upbeta+2)})$,
then $\updelta_n \asymp(1/n)^{1/(\upbeta+2)}$.
\end{longlist}

nodes.name: Theorem 2.3
nodes.statement:
Let $\Theta$ be a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$, $G_0,Q_0^* \in\mathscr{P}
(\Theta)$.
Suppose that assumptions \textup{(A1)} and \textup{(A2)} hold for some $r \geq1$.\vadjust{\goodbreak}
Given parameters $\upalpha\in(0,1], \upgamma> 0$, and
$H\in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ known. Assume further that:

\begin{longlist}[(a)]

\item[(a)] $G_0$ has $k < \infty$ support points in $\Theta$;
$Q_0^*\in\mathscr{P}(\Theta)$ such that $\operatorname{spt} Q_0^*\subseteq
\operatorname{spt} G_0$.

\item[(b)] For each $\tilde{n}$, there is a net $\updelta_{mn}= \updelta_{mn}(\tilde{n})
\downarrow0$
indexed by $m,n$ such that under
the model specifications (15), (16) and
(17),
there holds:

$\Pi_G (W_1(G,G_0) \geq
C \updelta_{mn}| Y_{[n]}^{[m]}, Y_{[\tilde{n}]}^0)
\longrightarrow0$
in $P_{Y_{[n]}|G_0}^m\times P_{Y_{[\tilde{n}]}^{0}|Q_0^*}$-probability,
as $m \rightarrow\infty$ and $n=n(m) \rightarrow\infty$ at a suitable
rate with respect to~$m$.
Here, $C$ is a constant independent of $\tilde{n}, m, n$.
\end{longlist}

Then, as $\tilde{n}\rightarrow\infty$ and then $m$ and $n=(m)\rightarrow
\infty$, we have

\[

\Pi_Q \bigl( h\bigl(Q_0*f,Q_0^**f
\bigr) \geq \updelta_{m,n,\tilde{n}} |Y_{[\tilde{n}
]}^0,
Y_{[n]}^{[m]} \bigr) \longrightarrow0
\]

in $P_{Y_{[\tilde{n}]}^0|Q_0^*}\times P_{Y_{[n]}|G_0}^m$-probability, where
the rates $\updelta_{m,n,\tilde{n}}$ are given as follows:

\begin{longlist}[(iii)]

\item[(i)] $\updelta_{m,n,\tilde{n}} \asymp(\log\tilde{n}/\tilde{n}
)^{1/(d+2)}+\updelta_{mn}
^{r/2}\log(1/\updelta_{mn})$.

\item[(ii)] $\updelta_{m,n, \tilde{n}} \asymp(\log\tilde{n}/\tilde{n})^{1/2}$ if $f$ is
